name: Mesomedes of Crete
bio: Mesomedes of Crete was a freedman and court musician of the emperor Hadrian in the second century AD. He is best known for a small group of lyric hymns, and Paton’s Index of Authors places him in the time of Hadrian.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XIV: 63; Book XVI: 323.

poems.title: Book XIV, 63: On the Sphinx
poems.author: Mesomedes of Crete
poems.text: A CREEPING, flying, walking maiden; a lioness lifting up feet not her own as she ran; she was a woman winged in front, in the middle a roaring lioness, and behind a curling snake. She ran away neither making a trail nor as a woman, nor either bird or beast in her whole body; for she seemed to be a maiden without feet, and the roaring beast had no head. She had an irregularly mixed nature, made up of imperfect and perfect parts.

poems.title: Book XVI, 323: On the Invention of Glass
poems.author: Mesomedes of Crete
poems.text: The workman having quarried it, brought the glass and put in the fire the mass hard as iron, and the glass, set afire by the all-devouring flames, ran out melted like wax. And to men it was a marvel to see a trail flowing from the fire, and the workman trembling lest it should fall and break; and on the points of the double forceps he put the lump.
